tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local derivation from the prior crash-window-A protocols. The slice specifies the minimum abstract API contract needed by either P1 independent fencing or P2 quiescent activation, then falsifies one deliberately weak primitive that provides only ordinary read plus unconditional last-write-wins put. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

minimum_authority_gate_contract.requirement: Expose one authoritative gate state containing at least mode(active or quiescent), monotonic authority epoch/fence, and a mutation version or equivalent compare token.

Support an atomic conditional state transition that succeeds only from the caller-specified predecessor state/version and cannot let an older epoch overwrite or resurrect authority after a newer epoch is committed.

Every protected side effect or authority-sensitive state mutation must validate the expected active epoch at the same linearization boundary as acceptance of that operation, or use an equivalent fencing-token primitive enforced by the protected surface. A separate read-then-effect check is insufficient.
For P2, quiescent(pending E1) must itself be authoritative and must reject effects from both E0 and E1 until active(E1) is committed. P1 does not require quiescence but still requires C3.
Protected effects must carry a stable logical effect key or idempotency key plus stable generation/payload identity so retry cannot create a second conflicting acceptance.

After interruption, timeout, or rate-limit response with unknown commit outcome, the caller must be able to read authoritative gate/effect state and distinguish committed, rejected, duplicate, and still-pending cases before retrying.
Successful transitions and guarded effect decisions must return or expose durable version/epoch/acceptance evidence sufficient for exact readback and deterministic replay reconstruction.

weak_primitive.assumptions: Even granting a linearizable single-key last-write-wins register, put has no expected-version/predecessor condition, no monotonic-epoch enforcement, and no atomic protected-effect guard.

falsification_trace: Initial authority value is active(E0). A stale claimant S and successor claimant N both read active(E0).
N unconditionally puts active(E1), intending to activate the successor epoch.
S, using its stale observation, later unconditionally puts active(E0). Because the primitive is last-write-wins rather than conditional/monotonic, E0 can become authoritative again.
Therefore W1 violates C2: it permits stale-authority resurrection after a newer epoch was committed.

Even if callers promise never to write a lower epoch, a protected side effect performed after a separate read of active(E1) can race with a later authority change before the effect commits. W1 provides no operation-boundary fence token or atomic guarded-effect acceptance, so it also violates C3.
For P2, a stale unconditional put can overwrite quiescent(pending E1) with active(E0), so W1 cannot guarantee C4 either.

Adding a stable effect key in caller data does not repair these authority races because W1 has no conditional acceptance primitive; concurrent or retried writers can still overwrite acceptance state without proving a unique winner.

observations: The prior abstract P1/P2 safety result depends on stronger semantics than ordinary storage: authority changes must be conditional/monotonic, and protected effects need a fence check coupled to effect acceptance rather than a separate pre-read.
A linearizable last-write-wins register is still too weak because linearizability orders writes but does not forbid a stale lower epoch from becoming the last write.
Quiescence is safe only when the quiescent state is itself authoritative and cannot be overwritten by a stale claimant without a failed predecessor/version check.
Stable idempotency keys are necessary for duplicate resistance but do not substitute for authority fencing.
inference: For the exact abstract model tested, any concrete Chat-exposed candidate for P1 or P2 must provide conditional monotonic authority transition semantics plus operation-boundary fencing or equivalent guarded acceptance; ordinary read plus unconditional last-write-wins storage is falsified even if single-key operations are linearizable. This narrows the unresolved provider search without claiming that any concrete provider satisfies the contract.
